data.name: Jonathon
data.long_meaning: The name Jonathon is derived from the Hebrew name ‘Yonah’ which means ‘Dove’ or ‘God has given’. In the Old Testament, there are several figures with this name, including a son of Saul and a priest in the time of Hezekiah. In the New Testament, there is a character named Jonathan who is mentioned in the book of Acts. Jonathon is a strong and noble name, often associated with kindness, faithfulness, and loyalty.

in_hebrew.name: יונתן
in_hebrew.long_meaning: יונתן הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'אלוהים נתן' או 'ה' נתן'. הוא מורכב משתי מילים: 'יונ' שיכולה להיות קיצור של 'יוה' או 'ה'', ו- 'תן' שפירושו 'נתן'. השם יונתן מוזכר בתנ'ך כבן של שאול, מלך ישראל, וחברו הקרוב של דוד המלך.

in_greek.name: Ιωναθαν
in_greek.meaning: Ο Θεός έδωσε ή Κύριος έδωσε
in_greek.long_meaning: Ο Ιωναθαν είναι η ελληνική μορφή του εβραϊκού ονόματος יונתן, που σημαίνει 'Ο Θεός έδωσε' ή 'Κύριος έδωσε'. Το όνομα αυτό αναφέρεται στη Βίβλο ως το όνομα του γιου του βασιλιά Σαούλ και του φίλου του βασιλιά Δαβίδ.

in_latin.name: Ionathas
in_latin.long_meaning: Ionathas est forma latina nominis hebraici יונתן, quod significat 'Deus dedit' vel 'Dominus dedit'. Nomen hoc in Biblia invenitur ut nomen filii regis Saulis et amici regis David.

in_english.name: Jonathon
in_english.meaning: God has given or Gift of God
in_english.long_meaning: Jonathon is a Christian name derived from the Hebrew name יונתן (Yonatan), meaning 'God has given' or 'Gift of God'. It is composed of two elements: 'Yon', possibly a shortened form of 'Yah' or 'YHWH', and 'tan', meaning 'to give'. The name Jonathon appears in the Bible as the son of King Saul and the close friend of King David. Throughout Christian tradition, the name has been associated with friendship, loyalty, and divine providence. Historically, the name has been popularized in various forms across cultures, including English-speaking countries.

biblical_reference.note: The name Jonathon is first mentioned in 1 Samuel 13:2 as the son of King Saul.
